subtopics.title: The Pulse — a Single Disturbance That Travels

questions.question: A pulse is best defined as:
options: A repeating pattern of crests and troughs
A single disturbance that moves through a medium
The rest position of a rope

questions.question: In a transverse pulse, the particles of the medium move:
options: At right angles — perpendicular — to the direction the pulse travels
Parallel to the direction the pulse travels
Along the rope toward the far end

questions.question: A knot in the middle of a rope, after a pulse has passed it, is found:
options: Carried along to the far end of the rope
Back at its rest position — the medium does a round trip while only energy travels on

questions.question: A pulse covers 6 m of rope in 2 s. A second, much larger pulse on the same stretched rope travels at:
options: 3 m·s⁻¹ — speed is set by the medium, not the size of the flick

subtopics.title: Amplitude, and What the Medium Actually Does

questions.question: The amplitude of a pulse is the:
options: Distance between the front and back of the hump
Maximum displacement of a particle of the medium from its rest position

questions.question: Amplitude is always measured from:
options: One end of the rope to the other
The crest of one pulse to the crest of the next
The rest (equilibrium) line of the medium to the point of maximum displacement

questions.question: A larger amplitude tells you that the pulse:
options: Carries more energy — but still travels at the same speed on the same medium

questions.question: A pulse travels at 3 m·s⁻¹. The time it takes to cover 4,5 m is:
options: 1,5 s — time equals distance divided by speed, 4,5 ÷ 3

questions.question: The principle of superposition says that where two pulses overlap, the displacement of the medium is the:
options: Displacement of the larger pulse only
Algebraic sum of the individual displacements — added with their signs

questions.question: A crest of plus 0,3 m overlaps a crest of plus 0,2 m. The displacement of the medium at that instant is:
A crest of plus 0,3 m overlaps a trough of minus 0,2 m. The displacement of the medium at that instant is:
options: Plus 0,1 m — the algebraic sum of plus 0,3 and minus 0,2

questions.question: After two pulses have overlapped and separated, each pulse:
options: Continues completely unchanged — original shape, amplitude and direction
Continues with half its original amplitude

questions.question: Constructive interference occurs when two pulses:
options: Displace the medium in the same direction, adding to a larger displacement
Displace the medium in opposite directions

questions.question: Two troughs of minus 0,2 m each meet. The result is:
options: A trough of minus 0,4 m — constructive interference, because the disturbances reinforce in the same direction

questions.question: A crest of 0,25 m meets a trough of minus 0,25 m. At the instant of complete overlap the rope is:
options: Momentarily flat — but both pulses still exist and emerge unchanged afterwards
Flat, and stays flat because the pulses destroyed each other

questions.question: Destructive interference produces a resultant that is:
options: Smaller than the larger pulse — opposite displacements partly or wholly cancel
Equal to the sum of the amplitudes ignoring signs

subtopics.title: One Flick of the Washing Line

questions.question: As the hump runs along the washing line, a peg on the line:
options: Slides along the line with the hump
Bobs straight up and down, then settles back where it hung

questions.question: The only way to make pulses travel faster along the same washing line is to:
options: Change the line — for example, pull it tighter

questions.question: What travels from your hand to the far end of the line?
options: The disturbance and the energy of the flick — the line stays where it is

subtopics.title: When Two Bumps Meet in the Middle

questions.question: Your 30 cm hump meets your friend's 20 cm hump. At the moment they fully overlap, the rope stands at:
options: 50 cm — the rope adds both heights

questions.question: Right after the meeting, the two humps:
options: Bounce back the way they came
Merge into one permanent tall hump
Pass through each other and carry on, each unchanged

questions.question: The complete story of any meeting of pulses has two scenes:
options: During the overlap, add the heights; after it, both pulses continue unchanged
During the overlap, the bigger pulse wins; after it, only the winner continues
During the overlap, nothing happens; after it, both pulses stop
During the overlap, the pulses swap sizes; after it, they return home

questions.question: An up-flick of plus 30 cm meets a down-flick of minus 20 cm. At full overlap the rope shows:
options: A little bump of plus 10 cm — plus 30 minus 20

questions.question: The one-line vocabulary rule for interference is:
options: Big pulses build, small pulses cancel
Fast pulses build, slow pulses cancel
Same signs build (constructive); opposite signs cancel (destructive)

questions.question: A 25 cm hump meets a 25 cm dip and the rope goes momentarily flat. The flat rope means:
options: Both pulses are still there, passing through — a moment later each emerges whole
The pulses are gone for good
